name: @groundbox/mcp

tools.name: create_sandbox
tools.description: Start a sandbox: a private Linux VM (Ubuntu 24.04 with git, Node, pnpm, Python and Docker) that you run commands in. Billed per second until it is deleted or its timeout passes. It is usually running when this returns; if the status is still queued or starting, run_command waits for it. With image it starts from a Docker image instead; the first sandbox from an image is waited for here while the image is turned into a disk (up to 5 minutes; a status still queued after that means it is not done: check list_sandboxes).

cpus.description: vCPUs, 1 to 16. Default 2. A team runs at most 2 sandboxes of more than 8 vCPUs at once

memory_gb.description: Default 2 GB per vCPU, at most 4 GB per vCPU

disk_gb.description: Default 20. A minimum: the disk is never smaller than the image's or template's own

timeout_minutes.description: Auto-stop after this many minutes. Default 60, at most 43200 (30 days)

on_timeout.description: What the timeout does. delete (default): the sandbox ends. stop: it is shut down and its disk kept (start_sandbox brings it back). pause: memory is kept too (resume_sandbox)

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Pause the sandbox (memory and processes kept, storage price only) after this many seconds with no activity, 30 or more. Activity is commands, file calls and open connections; CPU use alone is not. The next call that needs it wakes it. Left out: it runs until its timeout. Not with volumes

idle_cpu_percent.description: With idle_timeout_seconds: CPU use above this percent of one core counts as activity, for a background job that must not be paused

wake_on_request.description: With idle_timeout_seconds: false keeps an idle-paused sandbox paused until resume_sandbox. Default true

allow_hosts.description: Hosts the sandbox may reach, and nothing else: host names, wildcards, IPv4 addresses or networks, for example ["github.com", "*.npmjs.org"]. Left out: the open internet

deny_hosts.description: Hosts the sandbox may not reach, with everything else open: the same kinds of entry, for example ["*.tracker.example.net", "203.0.113.0/24"]. With allow_hosts too, a denied entry wins

secrets.description: Team secrets given to every command as variables of the same name, for example ["NPM_TOKEN"]. See list_secrets. The key needs the secrets:use scope

desktop.description: A desktop (Linux, Chrome) to drive with the computer_* tools: true for 1280x800

flex.description: Half price for work that can wait (batch runs, evals). It starts when a box has spare room, so it may stay queued for a while: list_sandboxes shows when it is running

snapshot_id.description: Start from a kept snapshot (keep_snapshot), snap_...: a new sandbox with that moment's memory, disk and running processes, also after the sandbox it was taken of is deleted. Leave cpus, memory_gb and disk_gb out: it has the snapshot's size. Not with template, image, volumes or desktop

template.description: Start from a template (create_template): its name, id, or name:version. Left out: the team's default template, else Groundbox's own image. Leave cpus, memory_gb and disk_gb out to get the template's size, which starts from its warm snapshot in well under a second; another size boots cold

image.description: Start from a Docker image, as docker pull takes it: python:3.12-slim, ghcr.io/org/app:tag, or an image in the team's Groundbox registry. Public images and the team's own registry only. Not with template. Commands run as root with the image's environment variables; its ENTRYPOINT and CMD are not run

volumes.description: Volumes (create_volume) to attach. A sandbox with volumes cannot be paused or forked

read_only.description: Default false. A volume is read-write in one sandbox at a time, or read-only in any number

idempotency_key.description: Send the same value when retrying, so a retry never starts and bills a second sandbox

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a command in a sandbox and wait for it. Give cmd (a shell line, run with sh -c) or args (a program and its arguments, run with no shell, so nothing in them needs quoting). Returns exit_code, stdout and stderr. A non-zero exit code is a result, not a failure of the tool. Commands start in the home folder; state on disk stays between commands, the shell's own state (cd, export) does not, so chain with && or pass cwd.

cmd.description: A shell line, for example "cd app && pnpm test". Give this or args

args.description: A program and its arguments, run with no shell, for example ["git", "commit", "-m", "Fix the bug"]. Give this or cmd

timeout_s.description: Kill the command after this many seconds. Default 60

max_output_chars.description: Keep this much of the end of stdout and of stderr. Default 30000

tools.name: start_command
tools.description: Start a command in a sandbox in the background and return at once with its exec_id: for servers, watchers and long jobs that run_command would wait on. The command runs on with nobody connected. Read what it printed with get_command_output, see it in list_commands, end it with kill_command. Give cmd (a shell line) or args (a program and its arguments, no shell).

cmd.description: A shell line, for example "pnpm dev". Give this or args

args.description: A program and its arguments, run with no shell. Give this or cmd

timeout_s.description: Kill the command after this many seconds. Default 3600

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: List the commands a sandbox runs and has run (with run_command, start_command or a stream), newest first: exec_id, the command, state (running, exited, lost), exit_code and duration_ms once it ended. running says how many run now.

tools.name: get_command_output
tools.description: Read what a command printed, from a position: seq 0 is the start, and the answer's seq is where to read on from. Returns stdout, stderr, done (the command ended and this reaches the end of its output), exit_code once done, and more (call again from seq now). It does not wait for new output.

exec_id.description: The command's id, from start_command or list_commands

seq.description: Read from this position. Default 0, the start

max_output_chars.description: Keep this much of the end of stdout and of stderr. Default 30000

tools.name: kill_command
tools.description: End a command in a sandbox by its exec_id, with everything it started. Sends SIGKILL unless another signal is given (SIGTERM or SIGINT let the command clean up).

exec_id.description: The command's id, from start_command or list_commands

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write one file in a sandbox, replacing it if it exists. Parent folders are made.

encoding.description: How content is encoded. Default utf8; use base64 for binary files

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read one file from a sandbox, up to 256 KB. For a larger file, read parts of it with run_command (head, tail, sed -n).

encoding.description: Default utf8; use base64 for binary files

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List one folder in a sandbox: name, type, size and modified time of each entry.

tools.name: make_dir
tools.description: Make a folder in a sandbox, with any parent folders it needs. A folder that is already there is fine (created: false).

tools.name: stat_file
tools.description: Whether a file or folder is in a sandbox, and its type, size and modified time. Answers exists: false when nothing is there.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Delete a file, a symlink or an empty folder in a sandbox. With recursive=true, a folder and everything in it. This cannot be undone. Nothing at the path is fine (deleted: false).

recursive.description: Delete a folder that has files in it, and all of them

tools.name: delete_sandbox
tools.description: Stop and destroy a sandbox and everything in it. Billing stops. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_sandboxes
tools.description: The team's sandboxes, newest first, with status, size and cost so far. Stopped and failed sandboxes stay listed: pass live=true to get only the ones that are not over.

status.description: Only sandboxes in this status, or in any of several: running, or [running, paused]

live.description: true: only sandboxes that are not over (every status but stopped and failed)

metadata.description: Only sandboxes whose metadata has every one of these pairs

tools.name: pause_sandbox
tools.description: Snapshot a running sandbox (memory and disk) and free its VM. A paused sandbox costs only storage. resume_sandbox brings it back as it was; with wake_on_request, so does the next call that needs it.

wake_on_request.description: True: the next call that needs the sandbox resumes it. Default false: it stays paused until resume_sandbox

tools.name: resume_sandbox
tools.description: Bring a paused sandbox back, with its files and processes as they were.

tools.name: stop_sandbox
tools.description: Shut a running sandbox down and keep its disk. Memory and running processes are gone; files stay. A stopped sandbox costs only storage and its status is shut_down (the status stopped means deleted). start_sandbox boots it again. To keep running processes too, use pause_sandbox.

tools.name: start_sandbox
tools.description: Boot a sandbox that was stopped with stop_sandbox, from its kept disk: the same id, files and settings, a fresh VM with no processes running. Billed per second again once it runs.

tools.name: fork_sandbox
tools.description: Copy a running sandbox into a new one with the same files and processes, in seconds. Set a sandbox up once (clone, install), then fork it for each agent or each fix you want to try. The original keeps running; each copy is billed on its own.

timeout_minutes.description: Auto-stop for the copy. Default: the original's

idempotency_key.description: Send the same value when retrying, so a retry never starts and bills a second sandbox

tools.name: set_egress
tools.description: Change what a running sandbox may reach on the network, without restarting it. allow_hosts: it reaches these and nothing else. deny_hosts: it reaches everything but these; with both, a denied entry wins. Entries are host names, wildcards ("*.example.com", every name under the domain), IPv4 addresses and networks. null removes a list; a list left out stays as it is.

allow_hosts.description: The new allowlist, or null for the open internet

deny_hosts.description: The new deny list, or null for none

tools.name: save_point
tools.description: Save the whole sandbox as it is right now (memory, disk and every running process) as a point you can rewind to later with rewind, or fork from with fork_universes. Takes well under a second after the first one. Returns the point's snapshot_id. Paid plan.

label.description: What this moment is, for example "before the migration"

tools.name: rewind
tools.description: Put a running sandbox back to a save point: its memory, disk and processes become exactly what they were then, and everything since is gone. Same sandbox id. Use it to undo a step that went wrong and try another way.

snapshot_id.description: The save point, snap_..., from save_point

tools.name: fork_universes
tools.description: Fork a running sandbox into many copies at once, all from the same moment (now, or a save point), each with every process still running. Each copy's commands see FORK_INDEX (0 to count - 1), so each can try a different thing. Waits until they are all up and returns the fork group with each copy's sandbox id. Up to 50 copies (more for internal teams); delete them all with delete_sandbox on each, or the API's DELETE /v1/fork-groups/{id}.

snapshot_id.description: Fork from this save point instead of from now

idempotency_key.description: Send the same value when retrying, so a retry never starts and bills a second sandbox

tools.name: keep_snapshot
tools.description: Keep a moment of a sandbox as a snapshot that outlives it: the sandbox can be deleted, and create_sandbox with snapshot_id starts a new sandbox from that moment (memory, disk and running processes) at any time. The moment is now (a running sandbox), or the save point snapshot_id (a running or paused sandbox). Waits until the snapshot is ready and returns it; its id is the snapshot_id for create_sandbox. Paid plan; storage is billed per GB-month like a paused sandbox. A snapshot no sandbox was started from in 30 days is deleted.

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox to keep a moment of

snapshot_id.description: Keep this save point (from save_point) instead of the moment now

label.description: What this snapshot is, for example "dependencies installed"

idempotency_key.description: Send the same value when retrying, so a retry never starts and bills a second sandbox

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: The team's kept snapshots, newest first: id, the sandbox each was taken of, label, size, whether it holds memory, when it was made and when it expires. Give sandbox_id for those of one sandbox.

tools.name: delete_snapshot
tools.description: Delete a kept snapshot. This cannot be undone. Sandboxes already started from it keep running; its storage is no longer billed.

snapshot_id.description: The kept snapshot, snap_..., from keep_snapshot or list_snapshots

tools.name: create_template
tools.description: Make a template: a ready-made disk that sandboxes start from, so they need no setup. The base is Groundbox's own image, a public image (python:3.12-slim) or a Dockerfile, plus apt, pip and npm packages, files and shell commands, built once. Sandboxes of the template's exact size (cpus, memory_gb, disk_gb) start from its warm snapshot in well under a second. Give wait=true to wait for the build (up to 10 minutes) and get its status and log; otherwise follow it with get_template_logs. Then pass template to create_sandbox.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the team

image.description: A public image, as docker pull takes it. Left out: Groundbox's own image (Ubuntu 24.04 with Docker, Node, Python, Go and the usual tools)

dockerfile.description: A Dockerfile's text, built with no context folder (COPY of local files fails; use files). Not with image

run.description: Shell commands run as root, in order, last; a failing one fails the build

env.description: Environment variables every command in its sandboxes gets

cpus.description: The size its sandboxes get and its warm snapshot is taken at, 1 to 8. Default 2

wait.description: Wait for the build to end (up to 10 minutes) and return its status and the end of its log

idempotency_key.description: Send the same value when retrying, so a retry never starts and bills a second sandbox

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: The team's templates: name, status (building, ready, failed), the version sandboxes get, whether it is the default, and the newest build with its size and whether it has a warm snapshot.

include_hidden.description: Also the hidden templates made for sandboxes created with image

tools.name: get_template_logs
tools.description: The log of a template build, with its status (queued, building, ready, failed, canceled). With follow=true, waits for the build to end (up to 10 minutes) and returns the end of the log; to read on from where you got to, pass after=next from the last answer.

version.description: The build's version. Default: the newest build

after.description: Only lines after this seq (next from the last answer)

follow.description: Wait until the build ends (up to 10 minutes)

max_output_chars.description: Keep this much of the end of the log. Default 30000

tools.name: create_volume
tools.description: Make a volume: a disk of its own that keeps its data after sandboxes are deleted. Attach it with volumes on create_sandbox: read-write in one sandbox at a time, or read-only in any number. A sandbox with volumes cannot be paused or forked. Paid plan; $0.08 per GB-month for its whole size.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the team; to attach it by name

idempotency_key.description: Send the same value when retrying, so a retry never starts and bills a second sandbox

tools.name: list_volumes
tools.description: The team's volumes: name, size, status, the sandboxes each is attached to, and storage billed so far.

tools.name: list_secrets
tools.description: The names of the team's secrets (API tokens, passwords) and when each was last used. Never their values: a secret cannot be read back. Give one to a sandbox with secrets: ["NAME"] on create_sandbox, and its commands get it as the variable NAME. A person sets secrets, in the dashboard or with `groundbox secrets set`.

tools.name: delete_volume
tools.description: Delete a volume and all its data. This cannot be undone. Refused while it is attached to a sandbox that is not stopped: delete that sandbox first.

tools.name: computer_screenshot
tools.description: A screenshot of a desktop sandbox (one made with desktop: true in create_sandbox), returned as an image. Coordinates for clicks are in the screenshot's pixels; with max_width the image is scaled, so pass coordinate_space with the size it reports.

max_width.description: Scale down to at most this width

tools.name: computer_click
tools.description: Click on a desktop sandbox at x, y (screen pixels). Returns where the pointer is, and a screenshot after the click unless screenshot is false.

tools.name: computer_type
tools.description: Type text on a desktop sandbox, as keystrokes into whatever has focus. Never type a password or a 2FA code: call request_handoff and let a person do it.

tools.name: computer_key
tools.description: Press keys on a desktop sandbox: "Return", "ctrl+l", "ctrl+shift+t", "alt+Tab", several separated by spaces.

tools.name: computer_scroll
tools.description: Scroll on a desktop sandbox, at x, y when given (else where the pointer is), by wheel clicks.

tools.name: computer_action
tools.description: Any computer-use action on a desktop sandbox, in the shape computer-use models emit: {action: 'left_click_drag', start_coordinate, coordinate}, 'mouse_move', 'hold_key', 'cursor_position', 'wait', 'clipboard_get', 'clipboard_set', 'open_url' {url}, 'wait_for_screen_change' {timeout_s}, and the rest.

tools.name: request_handoff
tools.description: Stop and ask a person to take over the desktop: to sign in, type a password or a 2FA code, or get past a challenge. Your input is refused until they give control back. Call wait_for_handoff next.

reason.description: What the person should do, shown to them

tools.name: wait_for_handoff
tools.description: Wait until the person gives the desktop back (or up to timeout_s). The answer's handoff.note is what they left for you. Take a screenshot next: the screen has changed.

tools.name: schedule_command
tools.description: Run a command on a schedule. Each run starts a fresh sandbox, runs the command and destroys the sandbox.

cron.description: Five fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * 1-5" is 9:00 on weekdays

timezone.description: IANA time zone the cron is read in. Default UTC

tools.name: list_ci_runs
tools.description: GitHub Actions jobs that ran on Groundbox runners, newest first: repo, branch, commit, status, result, seconds and cost.

tools.name: get_ci_logs
tools.description: The log of one CI job (the id from list_ci_runs or wait_for_ci). Logs are kept 7 days.

tools.name: wait_for_ci
tools.description: After a push, wait for that commit's CI to finish. Returns passed, failed (with the failing step's log) or timed_out. Give exactly one of branch, sha or run_id.

tools.name: get_ci_insights
tools.description: Per CI job on Groundbox over the last days (30 by default): runs, median and p90 time, queue wait, failure rate, flaky commits (failed, then passed on a rerun), minutes and cost a week, and CPU and memory used against the runner's size. A job with enough measured runs gets a right-sizing tip in plain words with the money, for example to move it to groundbox-2vcpu, or to a bigger size when it is CPU-bound.

repo.description: owner/name; every repo when left out

tools.name: get_ci_auto_sizes
tools.description: Jobs on Groundbox auto sizing (runs-on: groundbox, or groundbox-auto-<name> for a job's own runners) seen in the last 14 days: each job's label, the size picked for its newest run (any even size from 2 to 16 vCPU), the rule (start, hold, up_cpu, up_memory, down, floor) and the reason in plain words, its measured runs, average and peak CPU and memory, and the price a minute. Also the team's cap (settings.max_vcpus, 8 unless set) and what applies on its plan.

repo.description: owner/name; every repo when left out

tools.name: set_ci_auto_max
tools.description: Set the largest size Groundbox auto sizing may pick for the team's CI jobs: an even vCPU count from 2 to 16 (8 unless set). A higher cap lets a busy job get more cores and cost more a minute; a lower one caps cost. The key needs ci:write. Returns the cap and what applies on the team's plan.

tools.name: convert_workflow
tools.description: Rewrite GitHub Actions workflow files to run on Groundbox, as `groundbox migrate` does, and return the new text. Nothing is written and no git command runs: write and commit the result yourself. Pass every workflow file of the repo (path and full text), so each job's label is unique across them. source: the vendor the files use now (blacksmith, depot, namespace, github), or groundbox to move jobs on fixed Groundbox labels (groundbox-4vcpu and so on) to auto sizing. mode auto (the default) gives each job runs-on: groundbox-auto-<job id>, its own runners, with the size picked from its runs (a matrix keeps one label; a job id used in several files gets a name from its file in each, like groundbox-auto-deploy-api; with source groundbox, jobs on the shared label groundbox move too); fixed maps to the nearest fixed size. ARM, macOS and Windows runners stay as they are, with a warning. Per file: text, changes (line, from, to), warnings, and jobs (job id, new label, what it ran on, its vCPUs there). A vendor job's first auto run gets 4 vCPU; a job moved from a fixed Groundbox label starts at the size its runs of the last 14 days had.

default_vcpus.description: Fixed mode: the size for a label that does not say one (ubuntu-latest). Default 2

tools.name: get_flaky_tests
tools.description: Flaky tests in the team's CI on Groundbox over the last days (14 by default, at most 30), most flaky first. A test is flaky when it failed and passed on the same commit (two jobs, a rerun, or a retry inside one job) or keeps flipping between pass and fail on the default branch. Each has its file, suite and name, flaky_commits, flip_rate (share of its recent default-branch runs whose result changed), failures and runs, last seen, and a quarantine suggestion for the worst. The first few also carry their newest distinct failure messages and stacks (recent_errors), to find the cause. Use it to find and fix flaky tests: read the test, fix the race, shared state, timing or order dependence, and never just delete it.

repo.description: owner/name; every repo when left out

tools.name: search_ci_logs
tools.description: Search the team's CI job logs on Groundbox from the last days (7 at most), as the live log kept them. Every word of the query must start a word in the line, and the whole query must appear as written (any case), for example an error code, an exception, a test name or a file path. Returns the matching lines, newest job first, with the job, step, line number and two lines either side. Use it to see how often an error happens, when it started, and in which jobs.

q.description: Text to find, for example ECONNREFUSED or a test's name

repo.description: owner/name; every repo when left out

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: The team's balance in micro-dollars (1,000,000 = $1), usage this month, limits, the team's daily and monthly spend caps with what has been spent against them, and the key in use: its mode (a test key cannot start anything that costs money), scopes and its own spend caps. Work started past a cap is refused with spend_cap_reached.

tools.name: start_tuneup
tools.description: Ask for a CI tune-up of one GitHub repo (owner/name) the team's Groundbox GitHub App can see: an agent reads its workflows and build setup in a Groundbox sandbox and finds speed-ups (runner sizes, caching, parallel jobs, shallow checkouts). Free on the paid plan; one at a time, three a day. Takes a few minutes: poll get_tuneup. The person opens the one pull request from the dashboard.

tools.name: get_tuneup
tools.description: A CI tune-up: status (queued, running, ready, no_changes, pr_opened, failed), a summary, each change with its expected effect, the diffs, the pull request, and each job's time before and after once the pull request's CI has run.

tools.name: list_buckets
tools.description: The team's storage buckets (S3-compatible, on Groundbox's own disks): name, size and object count, the bytes used against the team's cap, this month's storage cost ($0.015 per GB-month, downloads free) and the S3 endpoint.

tools.name: create_bucket
tools.description: Create a storage bucket for files that should outlive a sandbox: build outputs, datasets, an agent's memory. Names are 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, and only need to be unique within the team.

tools.name: list_objects
tools.description: List objects in a bucket in key order. Give prefix and delimiter "/" to browse it like folders: keys under a deeper "folder" come back as prefixes.

tools.name: get_object
tools.description: Read one stored object (up to 256 KB here; larger ones: presign_url and download it, for example with curl in a sandbox).

encoding.description: utf8 (default) or base64 for binary objects

tools.name: put_object
tools.description: Store text (or base64 bytes) as an object in a bucket, replacing any object at that key. For big files, presign_url with method PUT and upload from a sandbox.

encoding.description: How content is written: utf8 (default) or base64

tools.name: delete_object
tools.description: Delete one object from a bucket. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: presign_url
tools.description: A URL that downloads (GET) or uploads (PUT) one object with no key until it expires: hand it to curl in a sandbox, a CI job or a person. Default one hour, at most 7 days. Anyone holding the URL can use it.

tools.name: signup
tools.description: Sign yourself up for Groundbox with no person and no card: you get an API key on a free trial ($1 of sandbox use; two sandboxes at a time, forks included, up to 2 vCPU, an hour each) and can test sandboxes on your own: save points, rewind, fork, pause and secrets included; kept snapshots, volumes and templates are not. Returns trial (credit and limits), claim_url and message_for_human. When you want more than the trial gives, send your person message_for_human: it asks them to open claim_url, take over the account and add a card. Needs no key.

agent_name.description: What to call you on the page the person sees

email.description: The person's email, if you know it. Stored only; nothing is sent to it

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tell the Groundbox team something did not work. The last failed call of this session (method, path, status, request id; no secrets) is sent along.

message.description: What happened and what you expected

instructions:
Groundbox gives you sandboxes: private Linux VMs you run commands in, billed per second.

Typical use: create_sandbox, then run_command as often as you like (git clone, install, tests), write_file and read_file to move files, and delete_sandbox when you are done. For a server or a long job, start_command runs it in the background and get_command_output reads what it printed. To give several agents the same ready environment, set one sandbox up and fork_sandbox it, or build it once with create_template and pass template to create_sandbox: sandboxes of the template's size start in well under a second. create_volume makes a disk that keeps data between sandboxes. After pushing to a repo that runs CI on Groundbox, wait_for_ci tells you pass or fail with the failing log. get_ci_insights shows each job's time, failure rate, cost and CPU and memory use, with right-sizing tips.

No key and no person at hand? Call signup: you get a key on a free trial at once and can test sandboxes yourself (save points, rewind, fork, pause and secrets included; kept snapshots, volumes and templates are not). When you want more than the trial gives (or a call answers trial_limit or trial_credit_exhausted), send your person the message_for_human it returns, with its claim_url: they take over the account and add a card.
